description: Next.js has a multi-layered caching system. With Cache Components (cacheComponents: true, the modern model), caching is controlled via the 'use cache' directive, cacheLife(), cacheTag(), revalidateTag(), updateTag(), and Suspense boundaries. Without Cache Components (legacy model), caching is controlled via fetch() options (cache, next.revalidate, next.tags), unstable_cache for non-fetch functions, and route segment config (dynamic, fetchCache, revalidate). The four conceptual cache layers are: Request Memoization (per-render deduplication), Data Cache (persistent across requests), Full Route Cache (static HTML and RSC Payload), and Router Cache (client-side in-memory RSC Payload). Understanding each layer's scope, invalidation mechanism, and interaction is critical for building correct and performant applications.

constraints.title: fetch() Requests Are Not Cached by Default in Modern Next.js
constraints.problem: In the current Next.js model, fetch() requests are not cached by default. Developers who assume all fetch calls are cached (from older documentation) will serve uncached, fresh data on every request, eliminating the performance benefits of static prerendering.
constraints.whyItMatters: Without explicit caching, every incoming request triggers a fresh fetch to the upstream data source. At scale, this means O(requests * data_sources) upstream calls, increasing latency, cost, and the risk of rate-limiting by external APIs. Prerendering opportunities are lost when data is not cacheable.
forbiddenPatterns: Assuming fetch() is cached without explicitly setting cache: 'force-cache' or next.revalidate
Fetching the same data in multiple components without using React.cache() for deduplication
Omitting 'use cache' directive when data is suitable for caching across requests
Using unstable_cache without understanding its invalidation semantics
allowedPatterns: fetch(url, { cache: 'force-cache' }) for data that rarely changes
fetch(url, { next: { revalidate: 3600 } }) for time-based revalidation (ISR semantics)
fetch(url, { next: { tags: ['tag'] } }) combined with revalidateTag() for on-demand invalidation
'use cache' directive with cacheLife() for both data and UI component caching
unstable_cache() for ORM/database queries in the legacy model
React.cache() for per-request memoization of non-fetch data sources
productionRisks: Excessive upstream API calls leading to rate limiting
High database load from uncached queries
Increased latency for every page request
architectureImplications: Every data fetch in a Server Component should have an explicit caching decision
Shared data (fetched in multiple components) must use React.cache() or 'use cache' to deduplicate
Static content should be fully prerendered; dynamic content should be wrapped in Suspense
optimizationGuidance: Classify all data as: static (cache indefinitely), time-sensitive (ISR with revalidate), user-specific (no cache or short cache with tags), or real-time (no cache with Suspense streaming)
Use 'use cache' with cacheLife('hours') or cacheLife('days') for content that changes infrequently
quickFixes: Add { cache: 'force-cache' } to fetch calls for stable data
Add { next: { revalidate: 3600 } } for hourly revalidation
Add 'use cache' to data functions or components that should be cached
architectureSuggestions: Establish a team convention: every data-fetching function must document its cache strategy in a comment
Create a central data access layer where caching decisions are co-located with the data fetching logic

invalid: export async function getProducts() { return fetch('https://api.example.com/products').then(r => r.json()) } // Uncached, runs on every request
valid: export async function getProducts() { 'use cache'; cacheLife('hours'); cacheTag('products'); return fetch('https://api.example.com/products').then(r => r.json()) }

constraints.title: Revalidation Must Be Triggered from Server Actions or Route Handlers Only
constraints.problem: revalidateTag() and revalidatePath() can only be called from Server Actions or Route Handlers, not from Server Component render functions.
constraints.whyItMatters: Calling revalidation functions during render creates a feedback loop: rendering triggers revalidation, which triggers re-rendering. This is prevented by Next.js, but attempting it causes errors. Proper cache invalidation is always event-driven (user action, webhook, scheduled job), not render-driven.
forbiddenPatterns: revalidateTag() inside a Server Component body
revalidatePath() inside a Server Component body
revalidateTag() inside a Client Component
revalidatePath() inside a useEffect
Calling revalidation during a GET Route Handler in response to read operations
allowedPatterns: revalidateTag('posts') inside a Server Action after a data mutation
revalidatePath('/blog') inside a Server Action after content update
revalidateTag() inside a POST/PUT/DELETE Route Handler (webhook receiver)
updateTag() inside a Server Action for immediate read-your-own-writes scenarios
productionRisks: Infinite revalidation loops degrading server performance
Stale data served if revalidation is called in the wrong context and silently fails
architectureImplications: Cache invalidation is architecturally tied to mutation events, not read events
The mutation → revalidation → re-render cycle is the core App Router data mutation pattern
optimizationGuidance: Always pair every Server Action that mutates data with the minimum necessary revalidateTag() calls
Prefer revalidateTag() over revalidatePath() for surgical cache invalidation to avoid unnecessarily purging cached routes
quickFixes: Move the revalidateTag() call into the Server Action that performs the mutation
For webhooks, create a POST Route Handler that calls revalidateTag()
architectureSuggestions: Define cache tags that map to business entities (e.g., 'product', 'user', 'post') and tag all fetches for that entity, enabling surgical invalidation with a single revalidateTag() call

invalid:
export default async function Page() { revalidateTag('products'); // ERROR: cannot call during render
const products = await getProducts(); return <ProductList products={products} /> }
valid: async function updateProduct(id, data) { 'use server'; await db.update(id, data); revalidateTag('products'); revalidatePath('/products') }

constraints.title: Runtime APIs Opt Routes Out of Full Route Cache
constraints.problem: Using runtime APIs (cookies(), headers(), searchParams) in a Server Component without Suspense wrapping causes the entire route to be dynamically rendered, disabling Full Route Cache (static HTML prerendering).
constraints.whyItMatters: Static routes are prerendered at build time and served from CDN with zero server compute cost. A single call to cookies() or headers() at the top level of a page forces every request to go to the server and re-render. This increases cost, latency, and server load at scale.
forbiddenPatterns: Calling cookies() at the top level of a layout.tsx (opts the entire app into dynamic rendering)
Calling headers() directly in a Server Component that could otherwise be static
Accessing searchParams directly in page.tsx without Suspense wrapping
Using dynamic route params without generateStaticParams when static generation is desired
allowedPatterns: Wrapping components that use runtime APIs in <Suspense> boundaries to enable Partial Prerendering (PPR)
Extracting runtime API access into a child component wrapped in Suspense
Passing runtime values as arguments to 'use cache' functions to parameterize the cache key
Using generateStaticParams() to statically generate dynamic route variants at build time
productionRisks: Entire app rendered dynamically because cookies() is called in root layout
Loss of CDN cacheability for routes that could be static
Increased server costs proportional to traffic
Higher TTFB for every request compared to a CDN-cached static response
architectureImplications: Root layouts should never access runtime APIs unless the entire app is intended to be dynamic
PPR (Partial Prerendering) allows mixing static shells with dynamic streamed components
The architecture goal is to maximize the static shell and minimize the dynamic portions
optimizationGuidance: Move runtime API access as deep into the component tree as possible
Wrap runtime API consumers in <Suspense> to leverage PPR and keep the outer shell static
Use generateStaticParams() for all known dynamic route values to enable static generation
quickFixes: Move cookies()/headers() calls from layout.tsx to a child component wrapped in <Suspense>
Extract the dynamic section into a separate component and wrap with <Suspense fallback={...}>
architectureSuggestions: Adopt a PPR-first architecture: design every page as a static shell with dynamic holes wrapped in Suspense
Treat dynamic rendering as an explicit opt-in, not the default

constraints.title: Router Cache Serves Stale Data Until Automatic Expiration
constraints.problem: The client-side Router Cache stores RSC Payload for visited routes and prefetched pages. After a Server Action mutation, the Router Cache may continue serving stale data on client-side navigation until it expires or is explicitly invalidated.
constraints.whyItMatters: The Router Cache is an in-memory client-side cache with a minimum 30-second stale time enforced by the client router. Mutations performed via Server Actions automatically invalidate the Data Cache and Full Route Cache, but the Router Cache requires a full page reload or explicit revalidation to clear, potentially showing stale data to users navigating between routes.
forbiddenPatterns: Expecting Router Cache to update immediately after revalidatePath() in a Route Handler (Route Handlers do not clear Router Cache immediately)
Relying on automatic Router Cache expiration for time-critical UX updates
Using router.refresh() as the primary solution for all stale data issues instead of proper revalidation
allowedPatterns: revalidatePath() and revalidateTag() inside Server Actions to clear Data Cache + trigger Router Cache invalidation on next navigation
router.refresh() from Client Components to force a fresh RSC Payload fetch
Hard navigation (full page reload) for guaranteed cache clearing
Using updateTag() in Server Actions for immediate expiration in read-your-own-writes scenarios
productionRisks: Users see stale data after mutations when navigating back to a page
Confusing UX: a user creates a post, navigates back, and does not see it
Difficult-to-reproduce bugs dependent on navigation history
architectureImplications: Server Actions are the preferred mutation mechanism because they automatically coordinate Data Cache and Router Cache invalidation
Route Handlers only clear Data Cache, not Router Cache
optimizationGuidance: Prefer Server Actions over Route Handlers for mutations that affect displayed UI
Use redirect() after a Server Action mutation to force a fresh navigation to the updated page
quickFixes: Add router.refresh() in Client Components after a mutation that must be reflected immediately
Call revalidatePath() from the Server Action after the mutation
architectureSuggestions: Design mutation flows as: Server Action → mutate data → revalidateTag() → redirect() to fresh route for guaranteed cache coherence

valid: async function createPost(formData) { 'use server'; await db.post.create({ data: { title: formData.get('title') } }); revalidateTag('posts'); redirect('/posts') }

constraints.title: Uncached Data Outside Suspense Blocks Prerendering (Cache Components Mode)
constraints.problem: When cacheComponents: true is enabled, accessing uncached or runtime data outside of a <Suspense> boundary or 'use cache' scope causes a build-time error: 'Uncached data was accessed outside of Suspense'.
constraints.whyItMatters: With Cache Components, Next.js enforces explicit handling of all data access patterns at build time. Any component that accesses non-deterministic or runtime data must either cache it ('use cache') or stream it (Suspense). This prevents accidental dynamic rendering of what should be static routes.
forbiddenPatterns: Accessing cookies(), headers(), or searchParams outside of a <Suspense> boundary without 'use cache'
Calling fetch() without 'use cache' and without Suspense wrapping
Querying a database without 'use cache' and without Suspense wrapping
Placing a <Suspense> with an empty fallback (null) at the root layout body, which defers the entire app to request time
allowedPatterns: Wrapping dynamic data consumers in <Suspense fallback={<Skeleton />}>
Using 'use cache' on data functions and components for cached prerendering
Using connection() before non-deterministic operations to explicitly opt into request-time rendering
Passing runtime values as arguments to 'use cache' functions
productionRisks: Accidental full-page dynamic rendering when only a portion needed to be dynamic
Performance regression from losing the static shell on routes that should be mostly static
architectureImplications: PPR requires every dynamic data access to be bounded by either Suspense or 'use cache'
The static shell is everything outside Suspense boundaries with 'use cache' components
An empty Suspense fallback at root layout opts out of the static shell entirely
optimizationGuidance: Always provide a meaningful fallback UI in Suspense boundaries — it becomes the static shell content
Use 'use cache' for shared, reusable data (blog posts, products) and Suspense for user-specific data (preferences, cart)
quickFixes: Wrap the component accessing runtime data in <Suspense fallback={<Loading />}>
Add 'use cache' to the function accessing the data if it is safe to cache
architectureSuggestions: Architect pages as: static header (no Suspense needed) + cached dynamic content ('use cache' components) + runtime user content (Suspense + streaming)

invalid:
import { cookies } from 'next/headers' export default async function Page() { const theme = (await cookies()).get('theme'); return
Content
} // ERROR in Cache Components mode: uncached runtime access outside Suspense
